environmentalTriggers.message: Immediate evacuation. Do not start engine. Ventilate area and contact emergency services.
Investigate source carefully. Ensure no ignition sources. Ventilate area.
Do not approach with open flames or spark sources. Isolate area and report.
Do not open hood. Evacuate immediately and call emergency services. Use a fire extinguisher if safe to do so.
Safely pull over, turn off engine, and investigate the source without opening the hood if smoke is present.
Immediate evacuation. Do not attempt to extinguish if large. Call emergency services.
Evacuate. High voltage and thermal runaway risk. Call specialized EV emergency services.
Do not touch. Risk of rupture and fire. Disconnect from power if safe, otherwise call a specialist.
Do not allow pets near the spill. Avoid skin contact. Clean up with absorbent material.
Identify the leak source. Contains toxic chemicals, wear gloves during cleanup.
Immediately ventilate the area. Shut off engine. Evacuate and seek fresh air.
Evacuate immediately to fresh air. Do not re-enter until area is cleared and source identified.
Avoid skin and eye contact. Clean thoroughly with appropriate absorbents. Dispose of waste properly.
Wear eye protection and gloves. Neutralize with baking soda. Rinse affected area with water.
Avoid inhaling. May cause frostbite on skin contact. Ventilate area.
Ensure adequate ventilation. Carbon monoxide risk is high. Do not run engine in enclosed spaces.
Disconnect battery immediately if safe to do so. Do not touch bare wires. Fire risk.
Do not approach. High risk of electrical shock and fire. Disconnect power if possible from a safe distance.
Wear gloves and eye protection. Neutralize corrosion with baking soda solution.
Indicates potential electrical issue or overheating. Safely pull over, turn off engine, and investigate carefully.

interactionHazards.message: Do not touch. High voltage components carry lethal current. Ensure proper lockout/tagout procedures are followed.
Treat all electric vehicle powertrain components as high voltage. Consult EV specific safety procedures.
Ensure engine is off and cool before working near fan blades. They can activate unexpectedly.
Keep hands and loose clothing clear of belts and pulleys when the engine is running or could start.
Do not work near these components without disabling the engine. Risk of severe injury.
Allow engine to cool completely before touching these components. Risk of severe burns.
Do not open radiator cap when engine is hot. Pressurized hot fluid can spray out.
Depressurize the fuel system before disconnecting any fuel lines. Fuel is highly flammable.
AC systems are under high pressure. Do not disconnect without proper tools and training to safely recover refrigerant.
Exercise caution around brake lines. Brake fluid is corrosive and the system is under pressure.
Disconnect the battery and wait for system discharge before working near airbag components. Risk of accidental deployment.
Handle these components with extreme care. Accidental activation can cause injury.
Ensure vehicle is properly supported on jack stands on a level surface. Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack.
Always use at least two jack stands when working under a vehicle. Ensure they are placed on strong chassis points.
Verify vehicle stability before working on brake components on a raised vehicle. Ensure wheel chocks are in place.
